record.context_brief: closing gems without rho3 or rho4 pairs
record.original_question: Suppose one starts with a gem of the compact 4-manifold consisting only of the handles of index at most two. Can one construct from it a gem of the associated closed 4-manifold even when the original gem contains no rho3-pair and no rho4-pair? More specifically, can one recognize or create the combinatorial structures needed to pass from the bounded handlebody stage to the closed manifold stage without assuming the special pair configurations used in Proposition 9?

evidence.quote: Another possible improvement would be to study how to obtain a gem of a closed 4-manifold, starting from a gem of the compact one consisting only of handles up to index two, even if no ρ3- or ρ4-pair appears in the latter (as assumed in Proposition 9).

The problem is obviously a difficult one, since it involves the combinatorial recognition of #m(S1 x S2) (m > 0) in 3-dimensional topology, but in specific situations it could possibly be faced, for example by detecting sequences of combinatorial moves yielding the desired ρ3-pairs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. An edge-coloured graph (Γ, γ) is a multigraph Γ together with a map γ : E(Γ) → {0,1,…,n} such that incident edges receive different colours. A gem (graph-encoded manifold) of dimension n is a regular (n+1)-edge-coloured graph that represents a piecewise-linear n-manifold by the standard construction in which each vertex is dual to an n-simplex and each c-coloured edge is dual to an (n−1)-face opposite the vertex of colour c. For a colour c ∈ {0,…,n}, a ρ_h-pair (h ∈ {1,…,n}) is a pair of c-coloured edges whose endpoints are joined by paths in suitably restricted residues, and whose cancellation by the elementary "ρ_h-move" produces a new gem representing the same manifold (in the closed case) or that allows one to fill in handles of higher index.

For compact PL 4-manifolds with boundary, a gem may represent a handlebody decomposition consisting only of handles of index ≤ 2. Closing such a 4-manifold (i.e. capping off its boundary with handles of index 3 and 4 to obtain a closed PL 4-manifold) requires recognizing that the boundary 3-manifold is a connected sum #_m(S^1 × S^2) for some m ≥ 0; combinatorially, this step has been carried out under the assumption that the gem of the bounded handlebody contains at least one ρ_3-pair or one ρ_4-pair.

Problem. Given a gem G of a compact PL 4-manifold M whose handle decomposition uses only handles of index at most two, devise a procedure to construct a gem G' of the associated closed PL 4-manifold M̂ (obtained from M by attaching 3- and 4-handles to ∂M, when ∂M is a connected sum of copies of S^1 × S^2) without assuming that G contains any ρ_3-pair or any ρ_4-pair. In particular, identify a sequence of combinatorial moves on G that either (a) produces an equivalent gem in which a ρ_3- or ρ_4-pair appears, or (b) directly yields a gem of the closed 4-manifold M̂, thereby providing a combinatorial recognition of #_m(S^1 × S^2) at the level of the boundary 3-gem.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. The question concerns combinatorially closing a gem of a bounded PL 4-manifold without the special ρ_3/ρ_4-pair hypothesis, which is intertwined with the open problem of combinatorial recognition of #_m(S^1 × S^2) among 3-gems; standard references on gem-complexity and crystallizations of 4-manifolds do not record a solution.

status_evidence.title: PL 4-manifolds admitting simple crystallizations
status_evidence.snippet: Simple crystallizations of 4-manifolds yield handle decompositions lacking 1- and 3-handles; closing procedures rely on detecting specific ρ-pair configurations.
status_evidence.claim: Existing closing procedures for 4-dimensional gems use ρ_h-pair structures, and a general procedure without them is not provided.
